text:
sara-ops: seeing a spike in p95/p99 for /v1/generate on us-east-1 around 11:02. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~820ms, p99 ~3.2s. multiple customers filing latency complaints. any oncall can triage? :eyes:

mike-sre: on it — pulling recent dashboards. can you paste an example request id or customer id? that helps route logs.

sara-ops: one customer id is acct_9b7f, sample request id: req_20260315_110220_7a3f. Happened across both small and medium models.

mike-sre: checking queue-depth + worker metrics now. running quick metric queries: `rcli metrics query --metric requests.queued --filter region=us-east-1 --range 10m`

deploy-bot: autoscaler event: "scale_up_requested" for pool inference-us-east-1-gpu at 2026-03-15T11:05:10Z (pending allocation).

nitya-ml: I see GPU utilization at 95% on a subset of workers and a growing pending queue on gateway pods. Looks like admission control is queuing instead of shedding.

alan-oncall: did admission-control start blocking or did it admit and then workers got overloaded (head-of-line blocking)?

mike-sre: logs show large numbers of `enqueue` events at the gateway followed by long wait times before dispatch. sample snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T11:03:44Z] gateway: req=req_20260315_110220_7a3f action=enqueue queue_pos=128 ttl=120s
[2026-03-15T11:03:47Z] gateway: req=req_20260315_110220_7a3f action=dispatch worker=inf-22 latency=1.2s
[2026-03-15T11:03:47Z] worker-inf-22: served req_20260315_110220_7a3f exec_time=1.9s gpu_mem=10.5GB
```

mike-sre: anecdote: many requests are small prompt but some have large max_tokens and are effectively monopolizing GPU time. admission controller is currently set to allow 1000 concurrent inflight per region, but worker concurrency per GPU is only 8. So queued requests pile up waiting for dispatch.

sara-ops: customers reporting p99 regressions even on short prompts. the hit to SLAs is real. urgent mitigation?

nitya-ml: short-term: we can enable request-shedding for low-priority/tier=free — return 429 for free tier for next 10m while autoscaler catches up. Also reduce region-wide `max_inflight` from 1000 -> 500 to prevent long queues.

alan-oncall: propose immediate mitigations (with commands):
1) flip `admission.shedding.free=true` via config rollout: `rctl rollout set admission.shedding.free true --region us-east-1`
2) lower gateway max_inflight: `rctl config set gateway.max_inflight 500 --region us-east-1`
3) temporarily increase worker concurrency for smaller models: `rctl set pool concurrency inf-small=12 --region us-east-1`

mike-sre: executing 1 & 2 now. monitoring effects.

deploy-bot: config-change accepted, rollout id=rb-776.

[~90s later]

mike-sre: after shedding free-tier and lowering max_inflight: queue depth dropped from ~1200 -> ~240 and p95 improved to ~260ms, p99 down to ~900ms. still above baseline but much better.

nitya-ml: good. medium-term mitigation: enable per-route token limits (reject requests with `max_tokens>1024` for non-enterprise) and add a quick path to route short prompts to a low-latency small-quantized model.

sara-ops: we should also notify affected customers with status page update. I'll draft a note: short-term degraded performance in us-east-1 for non-enterprise customers; mitigations in place; working on permanent fixes.

alan-oncall: long-term action items to reduce recurrence:
- implement admission controller that considers estimated execution time (estimate from prompt length + model) not just count.
- autoscaler: react to queue depth + pending allocation time (currently reacts to CPU/GPU utilization only). add a predictive scaler.
- per-customer QoS tokens and priority buckets.
- avoid single global max_inflight; use adaptive per-pool limits to prevent region-wide head-of-line queuing.

mike-sre: also we should add a graceful degrade response when queue wait > X ms: return `202 Accepted` with an async callback or stream an immediate low-fidelity reply (trim tokens) for lower tiers.

nitya-ml: I'll open a PR with admission-control change to compute `estimated_ms = base + prompt_tokens * per_token_ms` and use that to admit/reject. linking it to an integration test.

sara-ops: thanks team. I'll post an incident summary in #incidents and send the customer comms. tagging @product for prioritization of QoS work. :thumbsup:
